title: Maaya Rajeshwaran, 17, bows out of Chennai Open in quarter-finals after historic run
dek: The wild card, ranked No. 669, lost 6-3, 6-3 to former top-100 player Robin Montgomery after becoming the first Indian woman since Sania Mirza in 2012 to reach a WTA singles quarter-final.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi's run at the Chennai Open ended in the quarter-finals on Friday, when the 17-year-old Indian wild card lost 6-3, 6-3 to Robin Montgomery of the United States, a former top-100 player.

The defeat closed a week in which Maaya, ranked No. 669 in the world, became the first Indian woman to reach the quarter-finals of a singles event on the main WTA Tour since Sania Mirza at Pattaya in Thailand in 2012, according to the WTA. Only one other Indian woman, Shikha Uberoi in Kolkata in 2005, had reached that stage at tour level this century.

## The quarter-final

Maaya started well. In the fifth game of the first set she forced deuce on Montgomery's serve, earned a break point and took it when the American netted a backhand, according to reports from the match. But Montgomery, a left-hander now ranked No. 151, broke straight back with a two-handed backhand winner and went 4-3 up.

Maaya saved one break point in her next service game, but a double fault, her third of the match, gave Montgomery another chance, which she took after a return error. Montgomery served out the set at 6-3 and kept control in the second. Her first serve let her down repeatedly and blunted her attacking game, reports said.

Montgomery, who won a WTA 250 title on grass at 's-Hertogenbosch in the Netherlands in June, will play the top seed and defending champion, Janice Tjen of Indonesia, in the semi-finals. Tjen beat the sixth seed, Polina Kudermetova, 5-7, 6-4, 6-2.

## How she got there

Maaya entered the tournament on a wild card. In the first round she beat the eighth seed, Katarzyna Kawa of Poland, ranked No. 115, 6-4, 2-6, 7-6 (5), recovering from 5-2 down in the deciding set for her first win over a top-120 player. In the second round she beat a Polish qualifier, Weronika Falkowska, ranked No. 277, 6-4, 6-3.

The run follows her first professional title, a W35 event at Lagos in Portugal last month, which she won after coming through qualifying, according to the WTA. She first came to attention in February 2025 when, as a 15-year-old qualifier, she reached the semi-finals of the WTA 125 event in Mumbai. She is No. 16 in the world junior rankings.

She is the fourth player born in 2009 or later to reach a WTA quarter-final, the WTA said. Her week in Chennai is expected to lift her inside the top 500, according to reports.

## Other Indians

India's top-ranked woman, Vaishnavi Adkar, a 21-year-old wild card ranked No. 344, won her first main-draw match at WTA level by beating Britain's Jodie Burrage 3-6, 6-3, 7-5, before losing 6-3, 6-0 to the seventh seed, Anastasia Zakharova, in the second round. Sahaja Yamalapalli lost in the first round to Simona Waltert of Switzerland.

Maaya is still in the doubles, where she and Shrivalli Bhamidipaty reached the quarter-finals. Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale also reached the last eight.
